answers.question: Explain the difference between a process and a thread.
answers.answer: A process is an independent program in execution with its own isolated memory space (heavyweight), while a thread is the smallest unit of execution within a process, sharing memory and resources with other threads (lightweight)

answers.question: What is the CAP theorem?
answers.answer: The CAP theorem states that distributed data systems can only provide two of three guarantees simultaneously: Consistency (all nodes see the same data), Availability (every request receives a response), and Partition Tolerance (system works despite network failures). Because network partitions are inevitable in distributed systems, the trade-off is actually between Consistency and Availability (CP vs. AP)
